title: Admin console: network templates, KMS/HSM import and CLI-assisted onboarding notes
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures UX notes, wireframe ideas, and backlog grooming for two related admin console areas: reusable network template UX (VPC, subnets, peering, DNS) and secure key material import flows (KMS + customer HSM). Aim: a usable golden path for small teams and a powerful fallback path for enterprise/security teams who need CLI/terraform and BYO-HSM.

Audience:
- Product managers (private deployments)
- Console UX engineers
- Solutions eng / SE (onboarding playbooks)
- Applied infra/security for HSM requirements

Background/context summary (short):
Customers deploy Redwood Private into VPCs across regions and often need to bring their own KMS or HSM (FIPS, HSM appliances, cloud KMS with IAM constraints). Onboarding currently splits between console-guided flows and heavy docs for Terraform/CLI. We want to reduce support friction by surfacing network templates and a robust import flow (with verification, dry-run, and audit logs).

Goals (product + UX):
- Provide a small set of validated network templates (minimal, high-availability, transit/peered) with editable knobs.
- Let advanced users import existing infra definitions (CIDR blocks, route tables) via CLI/terraform snippets while keeping console visibility.
- Secure key import: support cloud KMS linking (IAM role delegation), KMS key import, and vendor HSM (pkcs11/bring-your-own-hsm) with stepwise verification and auto-generated remediation hints.
- Reduce first-week support tickets by 40% for private onboarding.

Constraints/assumptions:
- Customers vary widely; templates must be conservative (restrictive-by-default).
- We can call out to customer-managed endpoints for verification (e.g., test API on a bastion) but must not transmit secret material to Redwood.
- Audit logs must capture key actions (key import, KMS connection test, template edits) and be exportable via Console and API.

Golden path (single-team, small infra):
1) Console: Start a new Private deployment -> Choose region(s) -> Select "Use template" -> pick "Minimal-public-vpc"
2) Console shows a compact checklist with required subnets, NAT, route table summary, and security group defaults. Default labels to recommended values.
3) KMS step: "Link a managed KMS" -> choose AWS/GCP/Azure -> provide a role/credentials via temporary ARN + test button -> Console performs read-only test to confirm key alias and permissions -> user confirms.
4) Finalize -> deployment staged.
Notes: This path should take <15 minutes if infra exists or <30 minutes with guided template creation.

Enterprise path (BYO infra + HSM + compliance):
- Provide a "Bring your own" mode with three entry points: Console-guided import (for non-secrets metadata), CLI import tool (json/tfvars), and a verification-only dry-run API.
- HSM flow: allow customers to upload a signed metadata file from their HSM vendor (no private key material through the console). Offer an "operator-assisted" option where SE can run a short handshake with the customer to register slots and policies.
- Provide a stepper UI that splits responsibilities: Networking owner -> Security owner -> Infra owner. Each step can be approved/rejected and results in an audit entry.

Wireframe and UX microdecisions (bullets):
- Top-level stepper: Region(s) -> Network template -> KMS/HSM -> Review & Dry-run -> Approve & Provision.
- Template cards: show small ascii-diagram, estimated required subnet counts, and "change" button to expand editable fields (CIDR, AZ mapping, NAT mode).
- "Import existing VPC": file accept (json/tfstate partial), or paste tfstate snippet. UI will parse and highlight warnings (overlapping CIDRs, missing NAT, missing DNS resolver).
- KMS linking modal: 3 tabs: Cloud KMS (IAM role), HSM (PKCS#11/Conn string), Offline key import (signed metadata). Provide example commands for aws-cli/gcloud/az commands.
- Verification: Non-blocking background checks with clear success/failure cards and remediation hints (e.g., "Role missing kms:Encrypt permission — command to add: ...").
- Error UX: group errors by owner (infra, security) so messages route to correct person. Provide "copy remediation" button.

CLI/terraform-assisted onboarding notes:
- Create a small CLI tool (private-deployctl) that can export a "deployment manifest" for review in the console. Flow: user runs private-deployctl generate-manifest --from-terraform tfstate.json -> gets manifest.json -> uploads in console -> console runs dry-run checks and shows diffs.
- Include sample terraform snippets in docs and auto-generate tfvars in console when a template is selected.

KMS/HSM specific details (security focus):
- For cloud KMS we require a read-only verification role or temporary token. Console will only request test encrypt/decrypt permissions and will not retain credentials.
- HSM: Only support metadata registration via signed certificate. Offer two modes: "gateway mode" (customer runs an HSM gateway agent in their VPC that the Redwood control plane can query for status) and "offline registration" (most secure, SE-assisted).
- Key provenance: capture key fingerprint, key origin (imported vs generated), and key policy at registration time. Store only metadata + audit; never store key material.

Edge cases & failure modes to design for:
- Customer provides partial tfstate: parse errors should be surfaced as actionable lines, not raw JSON.
- Cross-region VPC with overlapping CIDR: show diagram and suggest NAT/transit gw architecture.
- KMS role created but missing kms:Sign (happens often) — offer in-console template IAM policy and one-click copy to clipboard.
- HSM outage during provisioning: rollback path must include orphan key registration cleanup and a remediation checklist.

Accessibility and internationalization notes:
- Stepper and templates must be keyboard navigable; all diagrams have alt text; avoid color-only error indicators (use icons + copy).

Backlog grooming / rough priorities (for next 3 sprints):
1) Sprint A (MVP): Template picker + minimal template card, cloud KMS link modal with test, basic audit entries, CLI manifest upload and dry-run UI. (High)
2) Sprint B: Import-from-tfstate parsing, advanced template edit, IAM policy snippet generator, error grouping by owner. (High)
3) Sprint C: HSM metadata registration flow (offline), gateway mode handshake, operator approval stepper, accessibility polish. (Medium)
4) Later: Terraform provider for Redwood Private that mirrors console templates and automated provisioning hooks. (Low)

Open questions (needs input from infra/security):
- How much of the verification handshake can we automate for vendor-specific HSMs? (Lars to scope with infra team)
- For audit retention, default retention period and export formats? (ask compliance)
- Should console allow users to schedule a provisioning window (time-of-day) to match maintenance windows? (ops input)

Next steps (action items):
- Evan: produce low-fidelity wireframes for the stepper and template cards (duedate 2025-11-22).
- Priya: draft KMS modal copy and IAM snippets for AWS/GCP/Azure (duedate 2025-11-24).
- Aisha: write CLI manifest spec and example tfstate parser rules (duedate 2025-11-27).
- Schedule 30min sync with SRE/security to walk through HSM gateway assumptions (owner: Aisha).

Notes-to-self / miscellaneous:
- Keep console logs of dry-run visible to user but redact any secrets.
- Try an experiment: pre-populate template with estimated cost delta (tokens + infra) to help customers choose dedicated vs hosted routing.

References: linked artifacts above; also see existing onboarding playbook PD-450 for field notes.

Unresolved UX detail: inline editing vs modal editing for template fields — lean modal for high cognitive load fields, inline for simple labels.

End of doc.
